issue.title: Reap finished or abandoned run_agent_runner processes instead of letting them poll for days

task_type_fields.proposal: run_agent_runner processes whose purpose is gone should exit on their own. On 2026-11-12 athena had 26+ runners alive (33 at report time, ~14 GB RSS): 27 WAITING + 2 QUEUED vs 5 RUNNING, five waiting since Nov 7 (sase-1r2.land, sase-1n6.11.land, the sase-1rq* land chain) and two QUEUED chop.refresh_docs.* burning 16-22% CPU each for a day. Proposal: give runners a liveness contract - a waiter periodically revalidates that its wait target (epic phase, gate, monitored command, queue slot) still exists and is still unsettled, and exits (releasing markers and slots) when the target is settled, canceled, or its bead/session is gone; optionally a host-side reaper audits runner PIDs against wait targets the same way. Any TTL must never kill an intentional long epic wait - target-revalidation, not wall-clock age, is the signal. Related stranding causes that leave runners orphaned: sase-1sh (staged monitor never adopted), sase-1si (dead phase worker leaves bead ownerless).
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Discovered while verifying and planning the fix for the sase TUI/runner capacity-scan CPU runaway. That epic (bound the runner-slot capacity scan; GC duty cycle) deliberately only makes waiting cheap; runner lifecycle/exit semantics touch wait adoption and host completion and need their own planning.

issue.creation_reason: Verifying the athena CPU report (tailnet--research athena_cpu_spikes_swap_and_runaway_sase.md) found 26-33 accumulated run_agent_runner processes (~14 GB RSS) with only ~5 agents RUNNING; the capacity-scan epic being planned makes their polling cheap but does not make abandoned runners exit.

payload.description: Staged-monitor adoption failures strand epic phases whose runners then poll forever; a runner liveness contract must treat this case
Dead phase workers leave in_progress beads ownerless; their waiters are exactly the abandoned runners this reaper should exit
